title: x-gap-mapping
description: A CSA gap mapping: one source requirement assessed against a set of target requirements, with a single coverage verdict for the set. An object rather than a relationship because the verdict is about the whole set — removing a target can change it — which makes the targets constitutive of the claim, and because a STIX relationship carries only one target_ref. Read source to targets: source_ref is what is mapped FROM.
$comment: gap_level is required because a gap mapping without a verdict asserts nothing, and target_refs is required and non-empty because a verdict with nothing to assess against is meaningless. Both are the substance of the claim rather than annotations on it.

source_ref.description: The requirement being assessed — what is mapped FROM. One object.

target_refs.description: The requirements it is assessed against, as a set. The verdict applies to the set as a whole, which is why these are one property on one object rather than several separate mappings that a consumer would have to re-merge to interpret.

gap_level.description: CSA's coverage verdict for this direction, assessed against target_refs as a whole. No Gap: the targets cover the source's requirement. Partial Gap: partial coverage. Full Gap: they do not cover it. These are the three values used across CSA's published mappings.

bidirectional.description: True when the assessment holds equally in the reverse direction. Coverage is not symmetric in general, so a reverse mapping is normally its own object with its own verdict.

description.description: Rationale for the mapping — the addendum text in CSA's published mappings, carrying scope qualification and caveats.
